# Partial diallel between two groups

\\ \newcommand{\mY}{\mathbf{Y}} \newcommand{\mT}{\mathbf{T}}
\newcommand{\mS}{\mathbf{S}} \newcommand{\mR}{\mathbf{R}}
\newcommand{\vg}{\mathbf{g}} \newcommand{\E}{\mathrm{E}}
\newcommand{\Var}{\mathrm{Var}} \newcommand{\Cov}{\mathrm{Cov}} \\

## 1 Abstract

When parents fall into two groups (for example lines and testers, or two
heterotic groups) and each parent of one group is crossed with each
parent of the other,
[`PartialDiallel()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/PartialDiallel.md)
gives the combining ability of each group and the specific combining
ability of the crosses.

## 2 The data

``` r

head(PartialDiallelData)
```

      Cross1 Cross2 Rep     y
    1      1     11   1 18.18
    2      1     12   1 16.40
    3      1     13   1 13.12
    4      1     14   1 17.71
    5      2     11   1 17.55
    6      2     12   1 18.05

``` r

with(data = PartialDiallelData, expr = table(Cross1, Cross2))[1:3, ]
```

          Cross2
    Cross1 11 12 13 14
         1  4  4  4  4
         2  4  4  4  4
         3  4  4  4  4

Ten parents (1 to 10) are crossed with four parents (11 to 14), in four
replicates.

## 3 The analysis

``` r

p <-
  PartialDiallel(
      y      = y
    , Rep    = Rep
    , Cross1 = Cross1
    , Cross2 = Cross2
    , data   = PartialDiallelData
    )
knitr::kable(x = p$ANOVA, digits = 4)
```

|        |  Df |   Sum Sq | Mean Sq | F value | Pr(\>F) |
|:-------|----:|---------:|--------:|--------:|--------:|
| Treat  |  39 | 144.7748 |  3.7122 |  2.7460 |  0.0000 |
| GCA I  |   9 |  58.5418 |  6.5046 |  4.8116 |  0.0000 |
| GCA II |   3 |  43.0531 | 14.3510 | 10.6158 |  0.0000 |
| SCA    |  27 |  43.1800 |  1.5993 |  1.1830 |  0.2654 |
| Error  | 117 | 158.1672 |  1.3519 |      NA |      NA |

``` r

knitr::kable(x = p$Genetic.Components, digits = 4)
```

|        | Components | Percent |
|:-------|-----------:|--------:|
| GCA I  |     0.3066 |  0.4044 |
| GCA II |     0.3188 |  0.2974 |
| SCA    |     0.0619 |  0.2983 |

With \\L\\ and \\M\\ parents in the two groups, \\\sigma^2\_{g^I} =
(MS\_{g^I} - MS_s)/(BM)\\, \\\sigma^2\_{g^{II}} = (MS\_{g^{II}} -
MS_s)/(BL)\\ and \\\sigma^2_s = (MS_s - MS_E)/B\\. `Percent` is each
source’s share of the treatment sum of squares.

## 5 Summary

Both groups show significant general combining ability; the specific
combining ability of the crosses is small.
